The post Baidu Releases ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base: A 280B MoE Base Model With 14B Active Parameters appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Baidu has released ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base , the raw pre-training checkpoint of its new sparse Mixture-of-Experts language model. ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base is a 280B-parameter text model from Baidu that activates 14B parameters per token. The weights stop at the end of pre-training, with no mid- or post-training applied. This as a clean starting point for teams that want to compare fine-tuning, instruction tuning or RL methods from one checkpoint. TL;DR Size: 280B total, 14B active per token; 128K training context, 1M for fine-tuning and inference. Runs on: Multi-GPU servers. Baidu’s reference configs use 4-way parallelism in SGLang and vLLM. GPU model and VRAM not disclosed. FP8 and BF16 weights. Performance: Best score on 24 of 30 base-model benchmarks in Baidu’s unified pipeline (self-reported). Best: MMLU-Pro 78.4, ahead of DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base at 69.2. Worst: HELMET-Rerank 56.2, behind DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base at 60.0. What is ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base? It is a text-only MoE base model with 43 layers and a 4096 hidden size . It was pre-trained from scratch on 33.5T tokens with the Muon optimizer. The tokenizer has 201,216 entries and groups numbers right-to-left in chunks of up to 3 digits. Activated compute, KV cache and long-context cost were treated as one budget. Pre-training data leaned on repository-scale code and long-context material, since those are hard to add later. How does the ERNIE 5.5 Flash architecture work? Hybrid attention : 37 layers use Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA), which caches 1 entry per 128 tokens. The other 6 layers use Multi-head Latent Attention with sparse attention (MLA + DSA). That means 1 in 7 layers keeps full-context access. HCA layers use 512-dim heads; MLA layers use 256-dim heads. Gated and mixed heads : The attention output gate comes from the low-rank query latent, cutting gate-projection parameters by 75%. Virtual Head Attention adds a lightweight low-rank mix across heads. Multi-Router Latent MoE. Each MoE layer has 512 routed experts (top-10) plus 1 shared expert. Several independent sigmoid routers replace a single router, per Baidu’s Multi-Router paper . Expert FLOPs and communication volume stay unchanged. Experts run in a 2048-d latent space, half the hidden width. ECHO instead of MTP. : ECHO reuses the backbone’s final layer to predict future tokens. The same layer doubles as a built-in draft model for speculative decoding. ECHO adds 0.36B parameters, excluded from the headline counts. Other pieces : The model uses Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections with expansion rate 4 and a MultiMax output head. How does ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base perform on benchmarks? Baidu team evaluated all 4 models with the same pipeline, prompts and few-shot settings. All figures below are self-reported by Baidu. Exams: MMLU 93.3, MMLU-Redux 94.1, MMLU-Pro 78.4. Knowledge: SimpleQA 34.1, versus 29.1 for DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base. STEM and reasoning: GPQA 60.2, MGSM 87.0, BBH direct 77.1. Code: HumanEval+ 82.3, MBPP+ 81.5, LiveCodeBench 40.1. Long context: RepoQA 91.7, LongBench-v2 48.7, HELMET-ICL 85.9. It loses on 6 tasks. DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base leads on ChineseSimpleQA, INCLUDE-lite, HELMET-Rerank and InfiniteBench. Hy3-preview-Base leads on BBH CoT and FullStackBench. Competitor numbers in Baidu’s pipeline differ slightly from each vendor’s own report. DeepSeek lists MMLU-Pro 68.3; Baidu measures 69.2. Tencent lists Hy3 MMLU-Pro at 65.76; Baidu AI measures 66.9. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index , it scores 31. Its predecessor, Inkling Small , scores 13 on the same index. The model is live on Tinker for fine-tuning and inference. Performance: 31 on the AA Intelligence Index, ranked #4 of 29 in its price class. Best: 86.3% on SWE-Bench Pro v2 (Hard), second only to Kimi K3 in the lab’s table. Worst: 13.1% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, versus 32.8% for GLM-5.3-Flash. What is Inkling 2 Small? Inkling 2 Small is a multimodal MoE model from Thinking Machines Lab for agentic coding, vision and knowledge work. It takes text and image input and returns text. It is important to note that it does not support audio as of now. Weights are closed at launch. The Thinking Machines Lab plans an Apache 2.0 release next week, after external safety testing and red-teaming. This follows its safe path to open weights policy. How is Inkling 2 Small built? It includes a 48-layer decoder-only transformer. Each token routes to 8 of 384 experts. Attention mixes local and global layers. A 292M-parameter vision encoder, based on Perception Encoder, uses 20×20-pixel patches with 2×2 spatial pooling. Image patches are interleaved with text tokens. Pretraining ran in 4 phases: H1: 8.4T tokens over 68 hours on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks, trained natively in NVFP4. H2: 3.8T tokens of newer, higher-quality data at 512K context. H3: about 320B tokens of reasoning and agent trajectories at 1M context. H4: about 34B tokens of the highest-quality agent trajectories. A single joint RL run followed. It took 1,075 steps, 17M+ rollouts and 9 days on 2,048 GPUs. Compute exceeded 4 × 10²³ FLOPs. Coding made up 65.0% of RL tokens. The previous Inkling used separate reasoning and agentic RL runs, merged by distillation. Alignment got explicit attention. Early checkpoints sometimes fabricated results and concealed actions on hard tasks. The Thinking Machines Lab added an alignment reward and on-policy self-distillation from a conduct spec.
